en: to answer / to reply / to respond
intro: Responder means to answer, to reply or to respond. It's a regular -er verb. You responder a alguém (answer someone) or responder a uma pergunta, a um email or a uma mensagem.

presente.en: I answer emails in the morning.
Why don't you answer my question?

presente.pt: O professor [responde] a todas as perguntas.
presente.en: The teacher answers all the questions.
We always answer in Portuguese.
They never reply to messages.

perfeito.en: I replied to your message yesterday.
Have you replied to the boss's email yet?

imperfeito.en: At school, I always answered first.
You used to reply to messages straight away.
He never answered letters.
We used to answer the questions in English.

futuro.en: I'll reply tomorrow morning.
The doctor will answer your questions.
We will reply as soon as possible.
Will you answer the questionnaire?

condicional.pt: Eu [responderia], mas não sei a resposta.
condicional.en: I would answer, but I don't know the answer.
What would you answer?
She would reply if she had time.
They would answer better in Portuguese.

presente.en: I always reply in Portuguese.
Why don't you answer?
She's answering the emails.
presente.pt: Ela está a responder aos emails.

perfeito.en: They didn't reply to my message.
perfeito.pt: Eles não responderam à minha mensagem.

imperfeito.en: He never answered letters.
We used to answer in English.
You always replied quickly.

futuro.en: I'm going to answer tomorrow.
Are you going to reply to the email?
We'll answer later.

condicional.en: What would you answer?
I would answer, but I don't know.
She would reply quickly.

notes.presente: Responder takes a: responder a alguém, responder a uma pergunta, responder ao email, responder à mensagem. The noun is a resposta (the answer).
notes.perfeito: Já respondeste? = Have you replied yet? Portuguese uses the perfeito where English often says 'have done'.
notes.futuro: In everyday European Portuguese you'll more often hear ir + infinitivo: vou responder, vais responder, vamos responder.

patterns.en: to reply to the email / the message

recap: Quando me perguntam alguma coisa, respondo sempre com um sorriso. (When people ask me something, I always answer with a smile.)

intro: Contar has two meanings: to count (numbers, money, people) and to tell (a story, a secret, what happened). It's a regular -ar verb. Contar com alguém means to count on someone.

quick.en: I'm going to count to ten.

presente.pt: Eu [conto] o dinheiro antes de sair.
presente.en: I count the money before leaving.
Do you tell your children stories?

presente.pt: A avó [conta] sempre a mesma história.
presente.en: Grandma always tells the same story.
We're counting on you for dinner.
They tell their parents everything.

perfeito.en: I've already told my mother everything.
Did you tell anyone the secret?
He told a very funny joke.

perfeito.pt: [Contámos] as pessoas na sala: eram vinte.
perfeito.en: We counted the people in the room: there were twenty.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, [contava] até cem em inglês.
imperfeito.en: When I was little, I used to count to a hundred in English.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [contava] histórias da guerra.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to tell stories about the war.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [contávamos] os dias até às férias.
imperfeito.en: We used to count the days until the holidays.
They always counted on us.

futuro.en: I'll tell everything tomorrow.
Will you tell the truth?

futuro.pt: O guia [contará] a história do castelo.
futuro.en: The guide will tell the history of the castle.
You will count the money at the end.

condicional.en: I would tell you, but it's a secret.
Would you tell your parents that?
He would never tell your secret.

condicional.pt: Nós [contaríamos] a história de outra maneira.
condicional.en: We would tell the story differently.

presente.en: I always tell my sister everything.
presente.pt: Conto sempre tudo à minha irmã.

presente.en: Can I count on you?
The children are counting to ten.
presente.pt: As crianças estão a contar até dez.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to tell stories.
I used to count the days.
They always counted on us.

futuro.en: I'm going to tell you a story.
Are you going to tell him?
We're going to count on you.

condicional.en: Would you tell your mother that?
I wouldn't tell anyone.
They would count on us.

notes.presente: Contar a alguém = to tell someone. Contar com alguém = to count on someone: Conta comigo! Use dizer for saying words; contar for telling a story, news or a secret.
notes.perfeito: Clitic after the verb: Ela contou-me tudo. After não, já, quando etc. it goes before: Ela não me contou nada.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: vou contar, vais contar, vamos contar.

recap: Conta comigo: não vou contar o teu segredo a ninguém! (Count on me: I'm not going to tell your secret to anyone!)

en: to say / to state / to affirm
intro: Afirmar means to state, to claim or to affirm. It's a regular -ar verb and more formal than dizer: you'll see it a lot in the news (o ministro afirmou que...).

quick.en: I can't say that for sure.

presente.pt: Eu [afirmo] que o trabalho está pronto.
presente.en: I state that the work is ready.
Are you saying you didn't see anything?

presente.pt: O jornal [afirma] que vai chover muito.
presente.en: The newspaper says it's going to rain a lot.

presente.pt: Nós [afirmamos] isto com toda a certeza.
presente.en: We state this with complete certainty.

presente.pt: Os médicos [afirmam] que o café não faz mal.
presente.en: Doctors say that coffee isn't bad for you.

perfeito.en: You said you were at home.

perfeito.pt: O ministro [afirmou] que os preços vão baixar.
perfeito.en: The minister stated that prices are going to fall.

perfeito.pt: Eles [afirmaram] que não sabiam de nada.
perfeito.en: They claimed they knew nothing about it.

imperfeito.pt: Antigamente, [afirmava] que nunca ia viver no estrangeiro.
imperfeito.en: I used to say I would never live abroad.

imperfeito.pt: Ela [afirmava] sempre que era a melhor.
imperfeito.en: She always claimed she was the best.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [afirmávamos] que o problema era simples.
imperfeito.en: We used to say the problem was simple.

imperfeito.pt: Os vizinhos [afirmavam] que a casa estava vazia.
imperfeito.en: The neighbours claimed the house was empty.

futuro.en: I won't state anything without proof.
The president will say the same tomorrow.
We will state what we saw.
They will claim it's true.

condicional.en: I wouldn't say that.
Would you say that in court?
Nobody would say otherwise.
Would you say that to the boss?

presente.en: The minister says that everything is fine.
presente.pt: O ministro afirma que está tudo bem.

presente.en: I can't say that for sure.
They claim it's true.

perfeito.en: She stated that she was at home.
perfeito.pt: Ela afirmou que estava em casa.

imperfeito.en: He always claimed he was right.
imperfeito.pt: Ele afirmava sempre que tinha razão.

imperfeito.en: They used to say the house was empty.
imperfeito.pt: Eles afirmavam que a casa estava vazia.

imperfeito.en: I used to claim I didn't like coffee.
imperfeito.pt: Eu afirmava que não gostava de café.

futuro.en: The president is going to say the same.
futuro.pt: O presidente vai afirmar o mesmo.

futuro.en: I'm not going to state anything.
Are they going to claim it's false?

condicional.en: I wouldn't say that.
Would you say that to your boss?
Nobody would say otherwise.

notes.presente: Afirmar is formal. In conversation you'll normally use dizer: Ele diz que... Afirmar is typical of the news, reports and formal statements.
notes.perfeito: Very common in news reports: O ministro afirmou que... (The minister stated that...). Similar verbs: declarar, garantir.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: vai afirmar, vão afirmar.

patterns.en: to be able to say (for sure)

recap: Posso afirmar com certeza que o português é uma língua bonita. (I can say for sure that Portuguese is a beautiful language.)

intro: Acontecer means to happen. It's a regular -er verb (with the spelling change aconteço), but in practice you'll almost always use the third person: acontece, aconteceu, acontecia. O que aconteceu? is one of the most useful questions you can learn.

presente.en: That happens to everyone.
Strange things happen in this house.

presente.pt: O que [acontece] se eu carregar neste botão?
presente.en: What happens if I press this button?
This happens a lot in winter.

presente.pt: Os acidentes [acontecem] quando as pessoas estão cansadas.
presente.en: Accidents happen when people are tired.

perfeito.en: A lot of things happened this year.
I don't know how it happened.

imperfeito.en: This used to happen every summer.

imperfeito.pt: Estas coisas [aconteciam] muito na minha aldeia.
imperfeito.en: These things used to happen a lot in my village.
What used to happen when it rained?
That never used to happen.

futuro.en: What will happen tomorrow?
That will never happen.
The changes will happen slowly.
The concert will take place at the Coliseu.

condicional.en: What would happen if we didn't go?
That would never happen here.
Without help, these things wouldn't happen.
Do you think that would happen again?

presente.en: What's happening?
That happens to everyone.
presente.pt: Isso acontece a toda a gente.

presente.en: It happens a lot in winter.

imperfeito.en: It used to happen every summer.
That never used to happen.
What was happening?

futuro.en: It won't happen again.
What's going to happen?
Nothing is going to happen.

condicional.en: What would happen if it rained?
That would never happen.
It would happen sooner or later.
condicional.pt: Aconteceria mais cedo ou mais tarde.

notes.presente: Acontecer a alguém = to happen to someone: O que te aconteceu? (What happened to you?) The subject often comes after the verb: Aconteceu uma coisa estranha.
notes.perfeito: O que aconteceu? and O que é que aconteceu? are the everyday ways to ask what happened. O que se passa? asks what is going on right now.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Não vai acontecer nada. O que vai acontecer?

compare.ex: O acidente ocorreu às dez horas.

recap: Aconteça o que acontecer, não vamos desistir. (Whatever happens, we won't give up.)

intro: Tratar means to treat (a person, an illness) or to deal with something. It's a regular -ar verb. Tratar de means to take care of / see to, and tratar alguém por tu means to address someone as tu.

presente.en: I'll take care of it tomorrow.
Do you call your boss tu?
The doctor treats a lot of patients.
We take care of the house paperwork.
They treat their customers very well.

perfeito.en: I've already dealt with the problem.
Did you sort out the tickets?

perfeito.pt: O hospital [tratou] bem a minha avó.
perfeito.en: The hospital treated my grandmother well.
Did you take care of the suitcases?

imperfeito.pt: Antigamente, [tratava] toda a gente por você.
imperfeito.en: I used to address everyone as você.

imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe [tratava] de tudo em casa.
imperfeito.en: My mother used to take care of everything at home.
We used to look after the animals on the farm.
They treated their employees badly.

futuro.en: I'll deal with it personally.
The lawyer will handle the matter.
We'll deal with your request tomorrow.
They'll take care of the party.

condicional.en: I would never treat someone like that.
How would you handle this problem?
She would take care of it, but she's ill.

condicional.pt: Nós [trataríamos] dos documentos, se fosse preciso.
condicional.en: We would sort out the documents, if necessary.

presente.en: I'll take care of it.
They treat the customers well.
What's it about?

perfeito.en: Did you sort out the tickets?

imperfeito.en: My grandmother took care of everything.
imperfeito.pt: A minha avó tratava de tudo.

imperfeito.en: He treated everyone well.
imperfeito.pt: Ele tratava bem toda a gente.

imperfeito.en: We used to look after the dogs.

futuro.en: I'm going to deal with the documents.
Who's going to take care of it?
We're going to take care of dinner.

condicional.en: I would never treat you like that.
How would you handle it?
She would take care of it.

notes.presente: Tratar de + noun = to take care of / see to: Eu trato do jantar. Trata-se de... = It's about... / It's a matter of... Tratar alguém por tu / por você = to address someone informally / formally.
notes.perfeito: Já tratei disso = I've already sorted it out. Clitic after the verb: Ele tratou-me bem; but Ele não me tratou bem.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vou tratar disso amanhã.

patterns.en: it's about... / it's a matter of...

compare.en: to look after / to care for

recap: Não te preocupes, eu trato de tudo! (Don't worry, I'll take care of everything!)

intro: Esperar means to wait, but also to hope and to expect. It's a regular -ar verb. Espera! (Wait!) and Espero que sim (I hope so) are everyday phrases.

presente.en: I'll wait for you at the door.
Will you wait here a minute?

presente.pt: Ela [espera] o autocarro todas as manhãs.
presente.en: She waits for the bus every morning.
We hope to visit Lisbon soon.
They're expecting a baby in May.

perfeito.en: I waited half an hour for the train.
He waited for us at the café.
We waited in the queue for an hour.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [esperava] por ela depois da escola.
imperfeito.en: I used to wait for her after school.
Were you expecting a different answer?
Nobody expected this.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [esperavam] o comboio quando começou a chover.
imperfeito.en: They were waiting for the train when it started to rain.

futuro.en: I'll wait for you.
The taxi driver will wait outside.
We'll wait until the end of the month.
Will you wait for us?

condicional.en: I wouldn't wait so long.
Would you wait for me?
She would wait one more day.
They would never expect that from you.

presente.en: I'm waiting for the bus.
I hope so.
We're waiting for you.

perfeito.en: They waited for us at the station.
perfeito.pt: Eles esperaram por nós na estação.

imperfeito.en: Nobody expected that.
I was waiting for the train.
imperfeito.pt: Eu estava à espera do comboio.

imperfeito.en: She used to wait for me after school.
imperfeito.pt: Ela esperava por mim depois da escola.

futuro.en: I'm going to wait for you here.
Are you going to wait?
We're going to wait until tomorrow.

condicional.en: Would you wait for me?
I wouldn't wait so long.
They would expect more.

notes.presente: Estar à espera de = to be waiting for (very common in Portugal): Estou à espera do autocarro. Esperar por alguém = to wait for someone. Espero que + conjuntivo = I hope that: Espero que estejas bem.
notes.imperfeito: Não esperava! = I didn't expect it! Use the imperfeito for what you were expecting or hoping in the past.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vou esperar por ti.

recap: Espera por mim, eu chego já! (Wait for me, I'll be right there!)

intro: Gostar means to like. It's a regular -ar verb, but it always needs de: gosto de café, gosto de ti. Don't forget the contractions: do, da, dos, das, disso.

presente.en: I really like coffee.
Do you like living in Lisbon?
She doesn't like fish.

presente.pt: Nós [gostamos] de ir à praia ao fim de semana.
presente.en: We like going to the beach at the weekend.

presente.pt: Os meus filhos [gostam] de jogar futebol.
presente.en: My children like playing football.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu não [gostava] de sopa.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I didn't like soup.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [gostava] de um café, por favor.
imperfeito.en: I'd like a coffee, please.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [gostava] muito de pescar.
imperfeito.en: My father really liked fishing.
They used to like walking in the park.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [gostarás] do Porto.
futuro.en: I'm sure you'll like Porto.
She'll like the present.
We will always like this house.
The kids will like the surprise.

condicional.en: I would like to book a table.
Would you like to come with us?
She would like to live in the countryside.

condicional.pt: Nós [gostaríamos] de falar com o gerente.
condicional.en: We would like to speak to the manager.

presente.en: I really like Portuguese food.
Do you like football?
We don't like waiting.

imperfeito.en: I'd like a coffee, please.
imperfeito.pt: Gostava de um café, por favor.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I didn't like vegetables.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era criança, não gostava de legumes.

imperfeito.en: My grandfather liked to read.
imperfeito.pt: O meu avô gostava de ler.

futuro.en: You're going to like it.
She's going to like the present.
I think they're going to like Lisbon.
futuro.pt: Acho que eles vão gostar de Lisboa.

condicional.en: I would like to book a table.
Would you like to come?
We would like to visit the Algarve.

notes.presente: Gostar always takes de: gosto de música, gosto do Porto, gosto disso. Gosto de ti = I like you / I'm fond of you.
notes.perfeito: Gostei! = I liked it (after an experience: a meal, a film, a trip). Gosto = I like it (in general).
notes.imperfeito: In Portugal, Gostava de... is the most common polite way to say 'I would like': Gostava de um café. Gostaria is a bit more formal.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vais gostar! (You're going to like it!)

recap: Gosto muito de aprender português, e tu vais gostar também! (I really like learning Portuguese, and you're going to like it too!)

intro: Adorar means to love or really like something: food, places, activities. It's a regular -ar verb and, unlike gostar, it takes no preposition: adoro café.

presente.en: I love custard tarts.
You love travelling, don't you?
My sister loves dancing.
We love summer in Portugal.
Children love ice cream.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [adorava] ir a casa dos meus avós.
imperfeito.en: I used to love going to my grandparents' house.
I'd love to go with you, but I can't.
She loved reading at night.
We used to love playing in the street.

futuro.en: You'll love this city.
Your mother will love the flowers.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [adoraremos] o espetáculo.
futuro.en: I'm sure we'll love the show.
You'll love the food.

condicional.en: I would love to visit the Azores.
You would love this restaurant.
He would love to come to the party.
They would love to meet you.

presente.en: I love Portuguese coffee.
She loves dancing.
Do you love the sea?

imperfeito.en: I'd love to go.
As a child, I loved chocolate.
They loved the beach.

futuro.en: You're going to love it!
She's going to love the present.
We're going to love this trip.

condicional.en: I would love to visit Madeira.
Would you love to live here?
They would love to meet you.

notes.presente: Adorar takes no preposition: adoro chocolate (but gosto de chocolate). It's stronger than gostar muito and very common for food, places and activities.
notes.perfeito: Adorei! is the typical reaction after a meal, a film or a trip.
notes.imperfeito: Adorava... = I'd love to... (very common and polite in Portugal): Adorava ir contigo.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vais adorar!

recap: Adorei Lisboa e tu também vais adorar! (I loved Lisbon and you're going to love it too!)

intro: Amar means to love, mainly for deep feelings towards people: a partner, your family, your children. It's a regular -ar verb. For things you love (food, places), people usually say adorar or gostar muito.

presente.en: I love my family.
Do you love your country?
She loves her husband.
We love our children.
The Portuguese love the sea.

perfeito.en: I loved once, many years ago.
Have you ever loved someone like that?

perfeito.pt: Ele [amou] a mulher até ao fim da vida.
perfeito.en: He loved his wife until the end of his life.
They loved each other for fifty years.

imperfeito.en: I loved that house.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [amava] a minha avó.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather loved my grandmother.
We loved summer in the village.
They loved animals.

futuro.en: I will always love this land.

futuro.pt: Tu [amarás] o teu filho mais do que tudo.
futuro.en: You will love your child more than anything.
He will love this city forever.
We will always love this house.

condicional.pt: Ele disse que a [amaria] para sempre.
condicional.en: He said he would love her forever.
Would you love someone who doesn't speak Portuguese?
I would never love a person like that.
Your grandparents would love this garden.

presente.en: I love you.
Do you love me?
We love our children.

imperfeito.en: My grandfather loved my grandmother.
imperfeito.pt: O meu avô amava a minha avó.

imperfeito.en: She loved that house.
I loved you.

futuro.en: I'm going to love you forever.
Are you going to love me forever?
They're going to love the baby.

condicional.en: He said he would love her forever.
condicional.pt: Ele disse que a amaria para sempre.

condicional.en: Would you love someone like that?
I would never love him.

notes.presente: Amo-te is strong and romantic. With friends and family people often say Gosto muito de ti. For things you love, use adorar: Adoro pizza.
notes.perfeito: Clitic after the verb: Ele amou-a. After não, já, nunca it goes before: Já te amei.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vou amar-te para sempre.

recap: Amo a minha família e adoro a minha cidade. (I love my family and I love my city.)

intro: Odiar means to hate. It's irregular in the present: the stem becomes odei- in every form except nós (odeio, odeias, odeia, odiamos, odeiam). All the other tenses are regular.

presente.en: I hate waking up early.
You hate the cold, don't you?
My brother hates vegetables.
We hate the Lisbon traffic.
Cats hate water.

perfeito.en: We hated the food on the plane.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I hated soup.
You used to hate maths.
He hated the noise of the city.
They hated waking up early.

futuro.en: I will never hate you.
In winter, you'll hate the rain.
She'll hate the noise.
They'll hate this music.

condicional.en: I would hate to live in a big city.
Would you hate working at night?
She would hate to miss the train.

condicional.pt: Nós [odiaríamos] ficar em casa o fim de semana todo.
condicional.en: We would hate to stay at home all weekend.

presente.en: I hate waiting.
Do you hate Mondays?
They hate the cold.

imperfeito.en: I used to hate vegetables.
He hated school.
We used to hate getting up early.

futuro.en: You're going to hate the rain.
She's going to hate this.
They're going to hate the traffic.

condicional.en: I would hate to live there.
Would you hate working at night?
She would hate that.

notes.presente: Odiar is one of a handful of -iar verbs that take -ei- in the present (except nós): odiar, ansiar, remediar, incendiar, mediar. Most other -iar verbs are regular: copiar → copio, enviar → envio. In conversation, detestar (to hate / can't stand) is also very common: Detesto esperar.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vais odiar isto.

recap: Odeio segundas-feiras, mas adoro sextas! (I hate Mondays, but I love Fridays!)

intro: Usar means to use. It's a regular -ar verb. It also means to wear (glasses, clothes) or to have your hair a certain way: uso óculos, usa o cabelo curto.

quick.en: I don't use it any more.

presente.en: I use my phone for everything.
Do you wear glasses to read?

presente.pt: Ela [usa] a bicicleta para ir trabalhar.
presente.en: She uses her bike to get to work.
We use a lot of olive oil in the kitchen.

presente.pt: Os alunos [usam] o dicionário na aula.
presente.en: The students use the dictionary in class.

perfeito.en: Did you use the credit card?
He wore a suit at the wedding.

perfeito.pt: [Usámos] o mapa para chegar ao hotel.
perfeito.en: We used the map to get to the hotel.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era nova, [usava] o cabelo comprido.
imperfeito.en: When I was young, I had long hair.
My grandfather always wore a hat.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [usávamos] cartas em vez de emails.
imperfeito.en: We used to use letters instead of emails.

imperfeito.pt: Antigamente, as pessoas [usavam] mais o comboio.
imperfeito.en: People used to use the train more.

futuro.pt: [Usarei] o carro só ao fim de semana.
futuro.en: I'll only use the car at the weekend.
You'll use this at work.
The company will use solar energy.

futuro.pt: Vocês [usarão] os mesmos livros no próximo ano.
futuro.en: You'll use the same books next year.

condicional.en: I would never wear that jumper.
Would you use an app to learn Portuguese?

condicional.pt: Ele [usaria] o carro, mas está avariado.
condicional.en: He would use the car, but it's broken down.

en: to carry out / to direct (a film)
intro: Realizar means to carry out, to hold (an event), to fulfil (a dream) or to direct (a film). It's a regular -ar verb and fairly formal. Careful: it doesn't usually mean 'to realise': for that, use perceber or dar-se conta.

presente.en: I direct short films.

presente.pt: Tu [realizas] o teu trabalho com muito cuidado.

perfeito.en: The doctors carried out the operation successfully.

imperfeito.en: I used to do all the work on my own.

futuro.pt: [Realizarei] o meu primeiro filme no próximo ano.
futuro.en: I'll direct my first film next year.

futuro.en: The school will hold a concert in June.

They'll carry out the building work in August.

condicional.en: I would direct a film about Lisbon.

We would hold the party in the garden.

presente.en: The town hall holds a party every year.
presente.pt: A câmara realiza uma festa todos os anos.

They would carry out the project.

notes.presente: False friend! Realizar = to carry out / to direct / to fulfil. 'To realise' (become aware) is perceber or dar-se conta: Percebi que estava atrasado. Realizar-se = to take place: O concerto realiza-se no sábado.
notes.perfeito: O realizador / a realizadora = the film director. O filme foi realizado por... = The film was directed by...
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vou realizar o meu sonho.

recap: Ela realizou o sonho de realizar um filme. (She fulfilled her dream of directing a film.)

intro: Abrir means to open. It's a regular -ir verb in all the tenses here; only the past participle is irregular (aberto: a loja está aberta). A que horas abre? is a question you'll use all the time.

presente.pt: Eu [abro] a janela todas as manhãs.

notes.perfeito: Nós abrimos is both present and perfeito; context tells you which: Ontem abrimos uma garrafa.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Vou abrir a janela.

intro: Fechar means to close or to shut. It's a regular -ar verb. You'll also use it for locking (fechar à chave) and for shops and businesses closing.

presente.pt: Eu [fecho] sempre a porta à chave.

notes.perfeito: Nós permitimos is both present and perfeito; context tells you which.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Não vou permitir isso.

patterns.en: to allow someone to do something

recap: Se o tempo permitir, vamos à praia amanhã. (If the weather allows, we'll go to the beach tomorrow.)

presente.en: I forbid phones at the table.

presente.pt: Porque é que [proíbes] os miúdos de brincar lá fora?
presente.en: Why do you forbid the kids to play outside?
The law forbids smoking in restaurants.

perfeito.pt: O governo proibiu os sacos de plástico.

intro: Ocorrer means to occur or to happen. It's a regular -er verb, more formal than acontecer, and mostly used in the third person. Ocorrer a alguém also means that an idea occurs to someone: Ocorreu-me uma ideia.

presente.en: This problem occurs often.

presente.pt: Os sismos [ocorrem] com frequência nos Açores.
presente.en: Earthquakes happen frequently in the Azores.

notes.presente: Ocorrer is formal (news, reports, notices). In conversation, use acontecer. Ocorrer a alguém = to occur to someone: Não me ocorre o nome dele (I can't think of his name).
notes.perfeito: Ocorreu-me = It occurred to me. After nunca, já, não the clitic goes before the verb: Nunca me ocorreu.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo, or simply acontecer: Vai acontecer outra vez.

recap: Ocorreu-me uma ideia: vamos jantar fora! (An idea occurred to me: let's go out for dinner!)

intro: Pensar means to think. It's a regular -ar verb. Pensar em = to think about; pensar que = to think that; pensar + infinitive = to intend / plan to.

presente.en: I think about my family a lot.

notes.imperfeito: Pensava que... = I thought that... (often a belief that turned out to be wrong): Pensava que eras português!

intro: Lembrar-se (de) means to remember. It's a regular -ar verb used with a reflexive pronoun: lembro-me, lembras-te, lembra-se... Without the pronoun, lembrar means to remind: Lembra-me de ligar à minha mãe.

notes.condicional: In speech, use proclisis after a trigger word (Nunca me sentaria ali) or the imperfeito: Sentava-me, mas...

recap: Senta-te, fica à vontade e bebe um café! (Sit down, make yourself at home and have a coffee!)

intro: Trabalhar means to work. It's a regular -ar verb. Use trabalhar em for a place or field, trabalhar como for a job and trabalhar para for an employer.

presente.en: I work in a hospital.
Where do you work?
My sister works as a nurse.

presente.pt: Nós [trabalhamos] a partir de casa às sextas.
presente.en: We work from home on Fridays.
My parents work a lot.

perfeito.pt: Ontem [trabalhei] até às nove da noite.
perfeito.en: Yesterday I worked until nine at night.
Did you work at the weekend?
He worked in France for ten years.
We worked together on that project.

imperfeito.en: I used to work in a bank.
You used to work near here, didn't you?
My grandfather worked on the land.

notes.presente: Trabalhar em (place / field): Trabalho num hotel. Trabalhar como (job): Trabalha como cozinheiro. Trabalhar para (employer): Trabalho para uma empresa alemã. O trabalho = work / job.
notes.imperfeito: Trabalhava num banco = I used to work in a bank (background, habit). Trabalhei num banco cinco anos = a completed period.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: Amanhã vou trabalhar.

recap: Trabalho muito durante a semana, mas ao domingo descanso! (I work a lot during the week, but on Sundays I rest!)
